# Didache Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_008_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 8

**1** When you fast, don't do it on the same days as the hypocrites. They fast on Mondays and Thursdays. You fast on Wednesdays and Fridays.

**2** When you pray, don't pray the way the hypocrites do. Pray the way the Lord taught in his Gospel:

> Our Father in heaven,
> may your name be held holy;
> may your kingdom come;
> may your will be done
> on earth as it is in heaven.
> Give us today the bread we need.
> Forgive us our debts,
> as we have forgiven those who are in debt to us.
> Do not bring us to the time of testing,
> but rescue us from evil.
> For yours is the power and the glory, forever.

**3** Pray this prayer three times every day.

---

*PNEUMA note: Chapter 8 is extraordinary. We are reading the Lord's Prayer as it was actually prayed in a first-century Christian community — in its living liturgical form. The doxology ("For yours is the power and the glory, forever") is not in Matthew's earliest manuscripts but is here, confirming that it was a liturgical addition that was in use by the time the Didache was written (c. 50-120 CE). Notice also: "debts" and "debtors" (matching Matthew, not Luke). The instruction to pray three times daily echoes Jewish practice (Ps 55:17; Dan 6:10) — this community was rooted in Jewish devotional patterns.*
